note: MEASURED the srmech Python suite end-to-end under WSL2 on native ext4 (HAS_NATIVE=True, .so built from the repo CMake, matching CI pip install -e .[dev]). HEADLINE: the suite is NOT uniformly slow - the ~150 ms/test framing is an artefact of dividing a skewed total by a flat count. Top 50 tests = 1467.2s = 64.0% of a 2292.8s run; the other 9,501 tests average 87 ms. ONE FILE, test_qm_so8_triality_c_rc146.py, is 453.3s = 19.8% of the entire suite from six tests. Second cluster is the thetasum family at ~277s across six files. The expensive head is native_equals_forced_pure differential tests, randomized soundness batteries, and whole-surface walks (test_immolation every-return-type 86.9s; test_mcp every-tool-invocable 31.5s) - i.e. it IS the coverage, which is why every proposal is scheduling/caching, never removal. Registration happens once per process at tool_schema import (sys.modules-cached) and warmup_all() is idempotent (0.07 ms/call) - there is NO per-module rebuild. Collapsing the pins is therefore explicitly NOT proposed: pure churn, no measurable win, and it would cost per-rc failure locality. BIGGEST LEVER, MEASURED NOT ESTIMATED: pytest-xdist -n 4 --dist loadfile = 897.4s vs 2618.1s serial on the SAME clean tree back-to-back = 2.92x (73% parallel efficiency), projecting the CI wall-clock driver 25.2 min -> ~8.6 min (~16.5 min saved per run). Cause located to exactly ONE LINE: test_bus_cipher_transport_c_rc179.py:97 parametrizes with os.urandom(2000) evaluated at COLLECTION time, so each worker process collects a different test ID and xdist refuses to start. One-line fix with zero coverage change (move the randomness into the test body, keeping per-run randomness and making the ID deterministic). Nothing else in 9,591 tests blocks parallelism. METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: my STATIC blocker audit (tmp_path discipline, ports, chdir/environ, ordering markers, ratchets) came back clean and WRONGLY cleared xdist as viable. Only RUNNING it found the real blocker. The static audit was necessary but not sufficient. PARALLELISM ALSO EXPOSED A REAL LATENT DEFECT: exactly one xdist-only failure, test_signal_processing_rfft.py::test_both_paths_registered - the file never calls warmup_all(), so it passes serially only because another module imported the registering path first. separate_finding_c_statics: FOUND WHILE CHASING THE ABOVE, reported as its own item: c/src/srmech_genome.c ~line 6099 carries four MUTABLE FILE-SCOPE statics - g_sc_arena (32 MiB), g_sc_slots (2^18 x 24B = 6 MiB), g_sc_win (64 KiB), g_sc_n_ids. MEASURED: the built library .bss is 39,911,536 bytes (39.9 MB), confirming these dominate its static footprint. THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) srmech_genome_section_counts() opens with memset(g_sc_slots, 0, sizeof(g_sc_slots)) = a fixed 6 MiB write PER CALL regardless of genome size, which dwarfs the real work on small fixtures (a per-call constant, not a leak, not quadratic); (2) NOT REENTRANT - four process-global mutables mean two concurrent calls corrupt each other, which sits uneasily beside the reentrant-C-core (#772) claim in docs/srmech/CLAUDE.md and is a hazard for any threaded host embedding libsrmech (safe under xdist, which uses processes); (3) 39.9 MB of BSS is paid by every process loading the library, including each xdist worker and each of the 36 test subprocesses. Looks like a consequence of honouring JPL Rule 3 (no dynamic allocation) by promoting buffers to file scope - a legitimate trade, but one whose cost and reentrancy consequence are currently undocumented. NO CHANGE PROPOSED; flagged for the C owner.
